transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm answer Johnson.
President Trump heads to Ohio today, taking his campaign into more competitive territory.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports the visit comes after stops in Republican-dominated states.
The president is traveling to Vandalia, Ohio, to support Republican Senator John Husted,
who is facing a tight race against Democratic former Senator Sherrod Brown.
Brown is seeking a comeback after losing his Senate seat, while Husted is a relatively
new incumbent.
He has served in the Senate for just two years after being appointed to fill the seat vacated
by J.D. Vance when Vance became vice president.
Ohio could offer an early test of how Republicans in swing states navigate Trump heading into
these midterms.
They can either embrace the president and use his ability to energize the Republican base
or create some distance from him to appeal to more moderate voters.
Trump is expected to travel to Nebraska next, another heavily red state.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News, the White House.
Group of seven nations have agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil from the reserves
as the price of diesel continues to rise.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports the decision comes after President Trump threatened to halt
diesel exports unless European countries tap their own stockpiles.
France chairs the G7, and President Emmanuel Macron convened the meeting by videoconference,
which included the head of the International Energy Agency, which is based in Paris.
Macron said the release would be coordinated by the IEA.
Macron said G7 members would also coordinate to increase production and bring down transport
costs like the insurance for tankers, he said, and push to get more tankers flowing through
the Strait of Hormuz.
That's NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reporting from Paris, according to AAA.
The national average for a gallon of diesel is $6.35.
The deal to merge Paramount's Skydance and Warner Bros. discovery is expected to become
final next week.
NPR's Mandalit Del Barco reports from Los Angeles.
With help from his billionaire father Larry Ellison and investors from Saudi Arabia, Qatar,
and others, David Ellison will soon have control over his mega company, which he named Skydance.
Ellison is spending more than $111 billion to combine two legacy film studios, streaming
companies and news outlets CNN and CBS News.
Ellison posted this video on X and wrote that Skydance will allow Paramount and Warner Brothers
to continue their individual identities.
Despite protests from actors, writers, and others, and after passing legal and regulatory
challenges, the deal is expected to close on Tuesday.
Mandalit Del Barco, NPR News, Los Angeles.
This is NPR News in Washington.
For the first time in history, the Kennedy Center Honors are being moved offsite to another
location in Washington, D.C., and NPR's Anastasia Seleucas reports the decision comes as the
legal fight over the performing arts center drags on.
The Kennedy Center Honors has been one of the institution's signature events since
1978, celebrating a wide array of American performing artists, from Al Pacino to Bruce
Springsteen to Yo-Yo Ma.
This year, the ceremony is moving away from the Kennedy Center, as President Trump and
his allies on the center's board have closed the complex for a major renovation, and Trump
has threatened to demolish it entirely if his name is not added to it.
The 2026 honors will be held on December 7 at Washington, D.C.'s Capital One Arena,
which seats 20,000, nearly 10 times as many as the award's traditional home, the Kennedy
Center Opera House.
Anastasia Seleucas, NPR News.
Former Miami Congressman David Rivera has been sentenced to 10 years in prison for his
role in a secret $50 million lobbying campaign on behalf of Venezuela.
The Republican and longtime friend of Secretary of State Marco Rubio worked for Nicolas Maduro's
government during the first Trump administration.
Rivera has been jailed since his conviction in May.
The jury found him guilty on all counts, including failing to register as a foreign agent and
conspiring to launder money.
I'm Windsor Johnston, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
